test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Name the first month of the national calendar of India based on the Saka Era which was adopted from 22 March 1957 along with the Gregorian calendar for the official purposes.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chaitra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• For the following official purposes, the national calendar based on the Saka Era, with Chaitra as its first month and a regular year of 365 days, was adopted on March 22, 1957, alongside the Gregorian calendar:
 
 
• Gazette of India.
 
• News broadcast by All India Radio.
 
• Calendars are issued by the Government of India.
 
• Government communications are addressed to the public.
 
 
 
• **Chaitra **is the Hindu calendar month. Chaitra is the first month of the year in both the Hindu calendar and the Indian civil calendar. Choitro is the Bengali name for the last month of the calendar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The month of Phalguna is on the Hindu calendar. Phalguna is the twelfth month of the year in India's national civil calendar and corresponds to February/March in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• Magha is the Hindu calendar month. It is the eleventh month of the year in India's national civil calendar, corresponding to January/February in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• Vaisakha is a Hindu month that corresponds to the months of April and May in the Gregorian calendar. Vaisakha is the second month of the year in the Indian national calendar.​
